title: Frequency-weighted fidelity budget — lab notes
body:
Purpose:

This note captures an exploratory spreadsheet design and recommendation heuristics for a frequency-weighted fidelity budget calculator. Goal: produce a lightweight workbook teams can drop into per-route cost analyses to answer the question: given per-token frequency and priority, how should we allocate INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit assignments (and dynamic fallbacks) to meet cost and latency SLOs while minimizing expected quality loss?

Background and motivation:
- Many workloads have non-uniform token importance: infrequent tokens (names, code tokens) are higher-utility for user-facing correctness, common tokens are cheap to degrade.
- Existing calculators tend to treat requests or entire sequences as monolithic: pick 1 quant profile for all tokens. We want a tractable middle ground: a per-route budget that can be expressed as a few knobs and mapped to scheduling/serving rules (e.g., per-segment precision, prefix caching, token-level fallback).

Assumptions (for spreadsheet model):
- Hardware profiles: A100-80GB and H100-80GB latency/cost baseline per token at FP16 (reference). We include multipliers for INT8/FP8/4-bit that reflect kernel speedups and GPU occupancy changes. (User-editable cells)
- Baseline quality metric: delta in cross-entropy (bits/token) or a task-specific metric (e.g., exact-match, F1). Model owners provide a measured fidelity penalty for each quant mode per token class.
- Token classes: high-value (top-k rare tokens), mid-value, and low-value (stopwords, punctuation). Frequency histogram input (percent of tokens in each class) is a required input.
- Batching and KV cache hit rate: two knobs that substantially change per-token latency and effective cost — included as inputs.

Key metrics and definitions for the sheet (single-line descriptions as spreadsheet column headers):
- Sequence length distribution (median, p95)
- Batch size (effective tokens per batch)
- KV cache hit rate (0–1)
- Token frequency split: %high, %mid, %low
- Per-token baseline latency_ms and cost_usd_per_1M_tokens at FP16
- Mode multipliers: latency_multiplier(INT8|FP8|4bit), quality_penalty(INT8|FP8|4bit) per class
- Per-class expected quality loss = class_fraction * quality_penalty(class, mode)
- Per-token effective cost = baseline_cost * latency_multiplier(mode) * (1 - cache_hit_rate * cache_savings_factor)
- Route-level expected quality loss = sum over classes per-token expected quality loss aggregated across sequence length and requests
- Budget constraint: max_allowed_cost_per_1M or max_avg_latency_ms

Sheet layout recommendation (tab-by-tab):
1) Inputs (single pane): hardware profile selection, baseline cost/latency numbers, batch/KV inputs, token distribution slider cells (percentages must sum to 1), allowable cost & latency SLO cells.
2) Mode profiles: table with rows INT8, FP8, 4-bit and columns: latency_multiplier, cost_multiplier, empirical_quality_penalty_high, _mid, _low, notes+source. Cells editable; defaults seeded from microbench runs (example numbers below).
3) Scenario engine: enumerates candidate assignments (per-class mode assignments). For three classes and three modes there are 3^3 = 27 candidate allocations; sheet enumerates all candidates and computes per-candidate: expected_cost_per_1M, expected_quality_loss, expected_latency_ms. Filter/sort by feasibility under SLOs.
4) Pareto frontier view: scatter of cost vs quality loss, pre-filtered by latency SLO; includes suggested knee points (where marginal cost per delta-quality increases above threshold).
5) Action mapping: textual mapping from chosen candidate -> runtime config snippets (example: "route: chat-complete -> assign prefix tokens (first 32) high fidelity FP8, body tokens INT8, enable on-fallback to FP16 for low-prob tokens").

Seed numbers (example defaults for workbook):
- baseline_cost_usd_per_1M_tokens (FP16): $20.00
- baseline_latency_ms_per_token (FP16 on A100, steady-state): 0.9 ms
- multipliers: INT8 latency_multiplier = 0.65, FP8 = 0.75, 4bit = 0.45
- quality_penalty bits/token (example measured): INT8 => [high: 0.012, mid: 0.004, low: 0.0008]; FP8 => [high: 0.005, mid: 0.002, low: 0.0004]; 4bit => [high: 0.035, mid: 0.010, low: 0.0025]
- cache_savings_factor = 0.7 (i.e., a hit avoids full re-compute by this fraction)
- Example token split: high 8%, mid 37%, low 55%

Calculation snippets (to paste into sheet formula cells):
- expected_cost_per_token(mode) = baseline_cost_per_token * latency_multiplier(mode) * (1 - cache_hit_rate * cache_savings_factor)
- expected_route_cost_per_1M = expected_cost_per_token(mode_for_class) * 1,000,000 * sum(class_fraction) [with per-class weighted average across sequence positions if prefix/body splits used]
- expected_quality_loss_route = sum_over_classes(class_fraction * quality_penalty(class, assigned_mode))

Scenario exploration examples:
- Candidate A (conservative): high=FP8, mid=FP8, low=FP8 -> cost ~ $15.0k per 1M (example), quality loss 0.006 bits/token
- Candidate B (aggressive cost): high=FP8, mid=INT8, low=4bit -> cost ~ $8.5k per 1M, quality loss 0.012 bits/token concentrated on mid tokens
- Candidate C (latency-first): high=FP8, mid=INT8, low=INT8 with permissive batch -> minimal latency, cost ~ $9.3k per 1M
(These are illustrative; users should run microbench to seed numbers)

Recommendation logic (heuristic rules for picking a candidate):
1) Respect hard latency SLOs first: filter candidates where expected_latency_ms <= SLO_latency_ms (uses p95 multiplier heuristic).
2) Respect cost target: filter candidates where expected_route_cost_per_1M <= budget_per_1M.
3) Among feasible candidates, sort by expected_quality_loss ascending. If none feasible, propose micro-actions: increase acceptable latency by X ms, accept hybrid fallback to FP16 for top-X% high tokens, or increase batch size and re-evaluate.
4) Knee point detection: compute marginal cost per unit quality improvement between adjacent candidates on sorted cost axis. Select candidate where marginal cost > team-defined threshold (e.g., $0.5 per 0.001 bits/token).

Runtime mapping and serving considerations (how to operationalize):
- Represent assignment as a small route config table: {route_id, token_partitioning: rules, mode_per_partition, fallback_policy}. Example rule: "tokens with model logprob < -6 run at FP16 for first 4 tokens after prefix; otherwise assigned class)."
- Implementation approaches: (A) static segmentation by token position (prefix/body/tail); (B) dynamic segmentation via on-the-fly token-scoring before decode (cheaper but needs fast scoring model); (C) post-decode inspection with re-score and re-run for high-risk tokens (expensive fallback). The sheet encourages teams to map chosen candidate to one of these three implementation strategies and estimate extra cost.

Edge cases and caveats:
- Highly-sensitive tokens may not be well-captured by frequency alone (PII, legal fragments). Flagging/explicit whitelists recommended.
- Small-context models (short sequences) make per-token switching overheads proportionally larger — spreadsheet includes a "switch overhead" multiplier to penalize rapid mode switches within sequence.
- Quant mode quality penalties are model-specific and non-linear vs seq-length. The workbook warns users to provide empirical quality deltas where possible rather than relying solely on our seed values.

Follow-ups and experiments to run (priority ordered):
1) Run microbench for H100/A100 to populate latency_multiplier and cost baselines for our top 6 models. (owner: Luis; due: 2024-11-08)
2) Collect per-token quality deltas from evaluation harness on 10k diverse prompts using importance-weighted sampling (owner: Aisha; due: 2024-11-20)
3) Prototype runtime config mapping for 2 routes (chat-completion and code-gen) and validate production latency impact in staging (owner: Connor; due: 2024-12-05)
4) Add a "simulated-request-batch" sheet that replays logged traffic histograms to produce an empirical expected cost distribution (owner: Ravi; due: 2024-12-12)

Action items (for this doc):
- Convert this note into a working Google Sheet template with tabs: Inputs, Modes, Scenarios, Pareto, Simulation, Runtime Mappings. (Maya)
- Link Sheet to the evaluation harness and microbench outputs using the linked_artifacts above. (Luis)
- Review with serving-runtime and console teams to ensure runtime knobs exposed by the sheet are implementable. (Review meeting: week of 2024-11-04)

Appendix: small pseudocode for enumerating candidates (to put in sheet script or notebook):
for mode_high in modes:
  for mode_mid in modes:
    for mode_low in modes:
      candidate = {high: mode_high, mid: mode_mid, low: mode_low}
      cost = sum(class_fraction[c] * cost_per_token(mode_for_class[c])) * 1e6
      quality = sum(class_fraction[c] * quality_penalty(mode_for_class[c], c))
      latency = base_latency_ms * weighted_latency_multiplier(candidate)
      record(candidate, cost, quality, latency)

Notes on weighted_latency_multiplier: use sequence position weight (prefix tokens might have lower batch efficiency) and add switch_overhead when candidate changes mode inside sequence.

Open questions (for group):
- What marginal cost threshold is product comfortable with for quality improvements? (requires GTM input)
- Should the default sheet prioritize minimizing worst-case token error (max per-token loss) vs expected loss?
- Do we want a "human-in-the-loop" toggle that auto-promotes high-value tokens to FP16 at the cost of a small budget reserve?

End of note.
